WITH macro_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_macro_count, SUM(usage_count) AS total_macro_usage_sum
  FROM macros
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
),
agent_reply_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_agent_reply_messages_2025
  FROM ticket_messages
  WHERE is_public = true
    AND author_agent_id IS NOT NULL
    AND created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  m.title AS macro_title,
  m.is_shared,
  m.usage_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * m.usage_count / NULLIF(mt.total_macro_usage_sum, 0), 2) AS pct_of_total_macro_usage,
  mt.total_macro_count,
  mt.total_macro_usage_sum,
  art.total_agent_reply_messages_2025
FROM macros m
CROSS JOIN macro_totals mt
CROSS JOIN agent_reply_totals art
WHERE m.deleted_at IS NULL
ORDER BY m.usage_count DESC, m.title ASC
LIMIT 20
note: Report is platform-wide (not tenant-filtered) since the question is about overall macro reliance across the library. usage_count is a lifetime counter with no date dimension, so pct_of_total_macro_usage and the constants are all-time, while total_agent_reply_messages_2025 is scoped to 2025 as a rough denominator only - the two are not directly comparable periods. total_macro_count reflects the full non-deleted library size so you can see concentration vs. the long tail beyond the top 20 shown.
